en: The eight rays of the sun on the Philippine flag represent the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish rule in 1896.
The National Mapping and Resource Information Authority officially counts 7,641 islands in the Philippine archipelago, which is 534 more than the previously accepted 7,107.
The Philippine Senate consists of exactly 24 elected senators who serve six-year terms, which is twice the three-year term of a House representative.
National hero Jose Rizal was a polyglot who could speak and write in 22 different languages, including Spanish, Latin, and his native Tagalog.
The Philippines celebrates the world's longest Christmas season, starting on September first and officially ending in January, spanning over four months of festivities.
The National Commission on Indigenous Peoples recognizes 110 distinct indigenous cultural communities across the Philippine archipelago, each with its own unique language and traditions.
National Scientist Fe del Mundo lived to be 99 years old, dedicating over 70 of those years to pioneering pediatric medicine in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, has a massive wingspan of up to two meters and stands about one meter tall.
Ferdinand Magellan arrived in the Philippines on March 16, 1521, marking the beginning of 333 years of Spanish colonial rule in the country.
Filipino citizens gain the right to vote in national and local elections at exactly 18 years of age, provided they are registered.
The Giant Lantern Festival in San Fernando features massive illuminated parols that can measure up to 20 feet in diameter and contain thousands of bulbs.
The 1898 Treaty of Paris officially transferred the Philippines from Spain to the United States in exchange for a payment of 20 million dollars.
